owner_approval: 2026-10-19, in chat: 'run merger arbitrage first, then the trend sleeve then A32 then A33'
why_this_stage: A stock-level merger-arbitrage backtest needs prices of acquired targets, and the project's price panel holds only 2 of 2,775 series that stopped trading -- acquired companies are missing (survivors only). That would silently bias any deal-level test, so it is blocked until a delisted-price source is available (Tiingo needs the owner's token). Real merger-arbitrage funds have long public records net of fees and costs, which answer the portfolio question directly: is this a different return stream, and does it improve the whole?
nature_of_test: A DIVERSIFIER test, not a signal test. A risk-transfer premium is judged on its economic rationale, its correlation and crisis behaviour over a long record, and what it does inside a portfolio -- not on a cross-sectional IC. No p-value is required, deliberately; the reading below is declared instead.

data.prices: Yahoo adjusted closes via yfinance, distributions included (checked: MERFX 2018 total +7.7% vs price-only +3.0%), month-end, through 2026-08 (the Fama-French RF series ends 2026-08)
data.risk_free: Fama-French daily RF compounded to months

measures.standalone: CAGR, volatility, Sharpe (excess of RF), max drawdown, beta and correlation to SPY, correlation in SPY's down months
measures.portfolio: replace 20% of the base with the fund, rebalanced monthly; Sharpe, max drawdown and CAGR against the base over the fund's full overlap and in each half of it; paired block bootstrap of the Sharpe change (block 12 months, 4000 draws) reported, not required

reading_declared_in_advance.family_representative: MERFX (longest record). ARBFX and MNA must agree in direction on the portfolio test or the family fails.
passes_if_all: MERFX monthly correlation with SPY below 0.50 over 1993-2026
in at least 5 of the 7 crisis windows MERFX either gains or loses less than half of SPY's loss
80% SPY/GLD/SHY + 20% MERFX has a higher Sharpe AND a max drawdown no deeper than SPY/GLD/SHY alone, over 2005-2026 AND in both 2005-2015 and 2016-2026
ARBFX and MNA, over their own overlaps, also raise the base's Sharpe
reading_declared_in_advance.if_it_passes: freeze a forward clock: 80% static SPY/GLD/SHY + 20% MNA (the cheaper, liquid ETF; MERFX is a mutual fund), weights fixed now, 52 untouched weeks, compared with SPY/GLD/SHY recorded from the same prices
reading_declared_in_advance.if_it_fails: close A30 stage 1; the deal-level stage stays blocked on delisted prices and should only be built if the owner supplies them

weight_note: 20% is Step 340's weight for the trend sleeve, reused so no weight is fitted here
trials_declared_here: one family reading (three funds as robustness)
known_weaknesses_declared_up_front: Fund returns are net of fees (MERFX ~1.2-1.5%/yr, MNA ~0.77%), so a do-it-yourself version could earn more -- or less, with worse execution.
The funds also hold stock-for-stock deals hedged with shorts; their return is not purely the long-only cash-deal design.
Survivorship: these are surviving funds; failed merger-arb funds are not in the sample.
